A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same M2A research despite the changed title and expanded authorship. Text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison throughout. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains a readable Appendix A.

before.justification: v1 reports original CTTA classification results on CIFAR10C, CIFAR100C, and ImageNetC, together with masking comparisons and ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports original classification, transfer, lifelong-adaptation, architecture, aquaculture, and semantic-segmentation experiments, including additional appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The frequency-masking procedure changes substantially: v1 selects individual bins using unshifted rectangular quadrants, whereas v2 defines radial bands with cutoff 0.5, masks conjugate pairs, and preserves DC/self-conjugate bins. These changes alter the generated views. The basic random-view schedule and consistency-plus-entropy approach remain.

E1.justification: The three original corruption benchmarks remain. v2 adds MRSFFIA-C fish-feeding-intensity recognition at severities 1, 3, and 5, plus CarlaTTA semantic segmentation across four driving-environment scenarios. It also evaluates transfer to corruptions withheld during adaptation.

E2.justification: The standard benchmark comparisons add RoTTA, DeYO, ROID, DPCore, and PAID, while removing v1's supervised upper-bound rows. The efficiency comparison also changes membership: ViDA disappears, while SAR, RoTTA, DeYO, and ROID are added.

E3.justification: The reported default ImageNet-C batch size changes from 20 to 64. New evaluation designs include adaptation on ten corruptions followed by testing on five held-out corruptions, ten-pass lifelong adaptation without resets, shuffled streams with inter-pass resets, seven-backbone comparisons, and task-specific segmentation and aquaculture training/evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: v2 adds lifelong-drift and ordering tests, GradCAM, t-SNE, corruption spectra, ranking-loss comparisons, patch-count sweeps, frequency-masking ablations, and very-small-batch tests. These investigate stability, mechanisms, and failure boundaries beyond v1's ablations. Conversely, v1's average-loss profiles, sample-fraction experiment, and explicit learning-rate sweep are absent.

E5.justification: v1 presents uncertainty values for M2A without identifying the run count or statistic. v2 explicitly specifies seeds 1, 2, and 3 and mean/standard-deviation reporting in Section 4.2. This clarifies the statistical procedure without establishing an increase in runs.

E6.justification: Reported patch-masking mean errors change from 8.3/19.8/39.2% to 8.9/19.8/37.4% across the three standard benchmarks; ImageNet-C has a changed batch size. Main frequency-result rows switch from all-frequency to low-frequency masking, preventing a direct performance-gain interpretation. Extensive new results include lifelong divergence and MRSFFIA-C ViT-L/16 errors of 28.5% for low-frequency versus 29.5% for patch masking.

T1.justification: The central mathematical frequency-mask definitions change from quadrant-based index sets to radial bands over conjugate pairs. Appendix A.3.2 adds explicit pair enumeration, self-conjugate sets, and Hermitian-symmetry reasoning; Section 3.3 introduces masked-domain expected risk. The consistency-loss rewrite is algebraically equivalent, and the structural-preservation account receives no formal theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v1 primarily claims a simple, effective CTTA method that avoids heuristic masking scores. v2 makes the systematic isolation of masking family its primary contribution, emphasizing cumulative stability and architecture/task-dependent recommendations. Comparisons with heuristic selection are explicitly demoted to suggestive, confounded evidence.

C2.justification: v2 develops a structural-preservation and spectral-overlap account beyond v1's spatial-bias and semantic-erasure explanations. It adds architecture/capacity explanations and conditions where frequency masking becomes competitive. Appendix A.7 acknowledges untested family–strategy interactions, unequal information removal at equal masking ratios, and conditional applicability.

D1.justification: v2 adds algorithm pseudocode, patch-placement/rejection-sampling details, conjugate-pair implementation instructions, layer-normalization update information, task-specific data preparation and source-training recipes, and measured adaptation times. However, v1's explicit statement identifying REM code and released source weights is removed, and the main text and appendix disagree on frequency-mask budgets.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially, including SPA, TCA, RoTTA, DeYO, ROID, DPCore, PAID, surveys, and task-specific references. Section 2 and Appendix A.1 reposition the contribution around masking family versus selection strategy, with extended comparisons to the mechanisms and conclusions of earlier masking-based methods.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and much of the interpretation are rewritten around two findings and family/strategy terminology. Related-work subsections are reordered, experiments are reorganized, and the standalone discussion is replaced by distributed interpretation and a revised conclusion. A structured appendix with a contents list is added.

P2.justification: v1's three benchmark tables become one multipart table, and its complexity table is redesigned around parameter percentages and elapsed time. Radar plots are redrawn, and ablation presentation shifts substantially toward per-corruption curves. New displays include a motivation diagram, activation maps, feature projections, spectra, segmentation examples, and sample trajectories.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens v1's narrow evidence for robust CTTA: lifelong and held-out tests directly examine stability and transfer, while architecture, segmentation, and aquaculture experiments establish important exceptions to the original conclusions. Explicit seeds, implementation recipes, and confounding limitations improve assessability. These gains outweigh the removed diagnostics and remaining reporting weaknesses, including conflicting frequency-mask budgets and the pixel-collapse description that overstates the CIFAR10-C findings in Table 2.
